transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-14
Time: 15:00 UTC (45 min booked, ran 55 min)
Duration: 55 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Raman (Redwood SE), Mark Sullivan (Sentinel Procurement), Aisha Khan (Sentinel Legal), Tom Becker (CTO), Lina Ortiz (Security)

Summary: quick procurement / legal alignment on MSA/DPA, discuss SLA asks, pricing approvals and next steps for onboarding/pilot. Agreed to circulate redlineable MSA + DPA and schedule technical deep dive for private deployment.

Topics: MSA terms, DPA data residency & encryption, SLA uptime and credits, pricing bands for hosted vs dedicated vs private, onboarding timeline, SOC 2 / pen test evidence, SSO/SAML and RBAC, KMS integration.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. we can do quick intros, i'm Jordan from Redwood, i run the account. priya is our systems engineer who's gonna cover the technical bits.
[00:15] Priya (Redwood SE): hi all, thanks. quick agenda - legal/procurement items first then tech questions and next steps.
[00:30] Mark (Sentinel Procurement): hey - we'll go round robin. primary goal today is to lock the MSA/DPA items and so the price approvers can sign off. timeline is tight, procurement wants final docs in two weeks.
[00:45] Aisha (Sentinel Legal): hi - quick note from legal: we need to see data processing terms, sub-processor list, data residency guarantees and the standard indemnity clauses. also curious re: SOC 2 and encryption at rest keys, how KMS is handled.
[01:05] Jordan: absolutely. we'll send a redline-friendly MSA and standalone DPA. Redwood maintains SOC 2 and we'll attach the report; for KMS we support customer-managed keys in our private offering, and hosted can be integrated with our KMS partner, we'll send details.
[01:22] Tom (CTO): for us, the bigger tech question is whether we run hosted or private. we have regulatory constraints for some PHI-like data - ideally private in our VPC or on-prem. priya - can you run through options?
[01:38] Priya: sure. we have Hosted API for easiest onboarding, Redwood Dedicated for reserved GPU capacity with isolation, and Redwood Private which can be deployed into your VPC or on-prem package. private gives you customer-controlled KMS, full audit logs, and no data egress to public tenants. note: private comes with different pricing and minimum commit.
[01:58] Mark: pricing - procurement needs a worksheet that shows per-token costs and any commitment discounts, also SLA credit structure. we might have to present to finance.
[02:10] Jordan: understood. we'll include hosted vs dedicated vs private columns. Also list burst policies, minimums, and a sample bill for your expected monthly tokens.
[02:22] Aisha: on SLA, we have a few asks: 99.9% for hosted endpoints, and 99.95% for dedicated/private, with clear credit calculations. do you have standard SLA wording?
[02:35] Priya: our standard SLAs are in the enterprise package; typical targets are 99.9 for hosted and 99.95 for dedicated. credits are pro rata based on downtime and request-level failure rates; we'll share the exact formula. caveat - regional outages and force majeure carve-outs are in there.
[02:54] Lina (Security): what about audit logs and retention? we need immutable logs for 12 months and ability to export to our SIEM, plus RBAC integration with our identity provider. also penetration test summary.
[03:10] Jordan: we can offer log forwarding to your SIEM and configurable retention. our enterprise package includes SSO via SAML/OAuth and role-based access. we'll attach SOC 2 report and pen test executive summary.
[03:25] Tom: firewall/networking - if we do private, what's the networking model? VPC peering, transit gateway, or on-prem colocation?
[03:35] Priya: Private supports VPC peering and a customer-managed transit setup; for on-prem we provide an appliance/containerized bundle. note that initial setup can take a couple weeks for network handshakes and key exchange. also KV cache behavior is different in private vs hosted - in private, prefix caching can be fully controlled by your routing team.
[03:56] Mark: procurement will require vendor risk questionnaire answered and the DPA to reflect data residency - specifically european data must stay in eu region, US data in us.
[04:08] Aisha: also, limitation of liability caps - we typically push for 2x fees or $5M, whichever is lower. what's Redwood's posture?
[04:18] Jordan: standard is a cap at fees for 12 months; we can discuss escalations for enterprise customers. we'll note this in the redline so legal can iterate.
[04:30] Priya: small note - some product names in our docs sometimes get munged, e.g., Redwood Dedicated sometimes appears as "Redwood Dedikayed" in auto transcripts, so please ignore typos in the attachments.
[04:45] Lina: encryption at rest - we need to know if keys are customer-managed in private, and rotation policies.
[04:52] Priya: yes, customer-managed keys in Private; hosted uses provider-managed by default but we can offer bring-your-own-key for enterprise customers with additional attestation. key rotation policy is quarterly by default; you can trigger rotations via API.
[05:10] Tom: on performance, we'll need typical p95 latency numbers and a cost/latency tradeoff for different quantizations. we do some real-time use cases.
[05:21] Priya: we have benchmark profiles; we'll share a short spreadsheet with p50/p95 for common models and recommended quantization. private typically has lower variance and better throughput due to dedicated GPUs and tuned kernels. caveat - batch sizing affects latency.
[05:40] Mark: procurement question - do you have a minimum term for Dedicated / Private? finance wants to know lock-in.
[05:47] Jordan: Dedicated and Private often come with a minimum commit (monthly/annual), but we can tailor. for pilots we can offer a short-term pilot with limited commit to validate before a larger reserved capacity purchase.
[06:02] Aisha: can you confirm sub-processors list and whether Redwood allows customer audits?
[06:09] Jordan: we'll include the sub-processor list. customer audits are supported for Private and enterprise relationships with standard notice and scope; in hosted we provide third-party audit reports (SOC 2).
[06:22] Lina: also need to confirm data deletion guarantees after termination and e-discovery support.
[06:30] Priya: data deletion is supported - DPA will include retention and deletion timelines. we also provide export tools for e-discovery.
[06:42] Mark: ok, next steps: we'll need the docs and a pricing sheet to route to finance; legal will redline MSA/DPA and come back. if possible include a sample SLA clause and an onboarding runbook.
[06:58] Jordan: yes - Jordan to send docs; priya to prep tech deep dive. we'll aim to send within three business days.
[07:10] Aisha: timeline - legal will try to return redlines within 10 business days once we have the draft; procurement needs final sign-off by 10/28 if possible.
[07:22] Tom: schedule the tech deep dive for next week (week of 10/19) - we'll confirm availability via calendar.
[07:34] Priya: quick clarifying Q on keys - do you need HSM-backed keys?
[07:38] Lina: yes - for PHI we require HSM-backed KMS in private; verify attestation.
[07:44] Priya: noted, we'll include details on HSM options and attestation docs.
[07:52] Jordan: any blockers from procurement/finance we should know?
[07:56] Mark: main risk is the SLA and liability caps; finance and legal will push on both. if you can provide precedent language or higher caps for enterprise plan that helps.
[08:08] Jordan: understood - we'll surface options in the redline.
[08:15] Aisha: also, please include a list of subcontractors and whether any processing occurs in third countries.
[08:22] Jordan: yes, sub-processor list will be included.
[08:28] Tom: ok, that's it from the tech side.
[08:32] Jordan: recap of next steps: Jordan send MSA/DPA + pricing worksheet + SOC2 and pen test exec summary by 2026-10-17; Priya schedule and prepare technical deep dive for 10/19-10/23 window; Sentinel to send security checklist and confirm pilot scope.
[08:50] Aisha: thanks all.
[08:53] Mark: thanks.
[08:55] Jordan: thanks everyone - we'll follow up in email.

Meeting end.
